 'Disappointing result, but fair' published at 22:43 GMT 31 October 22:43 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham 
 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa head coach Unai Emery speaking to BBC MOTD: "Disappointing result, but fair. The first half, we tried to dominate the match, to break their high build-up with the press. We did it more times than less. Sometimes, they could break our press and they created one or two chances but saved Zion Suzuki. We were creating chances, we were creating goals. We had a penalty shot. We scored a goal. In the first half, we more or less were [there]. Tough match, but we were more or less feeling comfortable. We wanted to carry on the second half in the same way, but we couldn't. I don't know why, but we couldn't. They were demanding it more, they were pushing more. They were creating chances more. We were defending. They scored the goal. They threw enough at it. It changed a bit. We started the game pushing, not being organised like we were but pushing. We created two or three chances to score the goal. I think the result is a fair result. Disappointing for us. Not enough, but we keep going forward."
 On Suzuki's mistake for the goal: "Yes, but it's part of football. 
 "Keeping going forward. Keep improving. Today was about a very good test, but we need to continue working and improving things. Work to do. Try to adapt our players to get better, get confidence. Plus, we are improving our results. In our last five matches in the Premier League, three won, two draws. I think it is good, but our poor start is giving us a lack of points in the table. Today improving. A draw is a disappointing result, but a fair result but we must keep going. Next challenge is Tuesday against Barcelona. Next challenge is against Manchester United, so it's not time to stop. It's not time to be focussing on what was before. Our focus is the next match, next days. Each competition is giving us a lot of moments tot y to build the team. We are building and we are working to improve."
 On next two matches : "Yes, difficult. Every match."
 On going to Barcelona on his birthday : "We are looking forward to it."
 24 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'My players showed ambition and character' published at 22:40 GMT 31 October 22:40 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham 
 Fulham 
 Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "Yes, of course [being pleased with his team's performance] especially in the second half. We were more aggressive, we controlled the tempo of the game, we had so many chances to score some goals, but in the end we couldn't take the chances.
 "I am happy because we knew before the match how difficult it would be to win here. Manchester City lost here one week ago and they are a Champions League team with a fantastic coach, so, for me I'm really proud of my players because they showed ambition and character, and we played our way, which is the most important thing."
 On Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki: "He is a fantastic keeper, and I think he did really well tonight. He was unlucky in our goal but he saved two or three goals for Villa before."
 On being defensively solid: "I think we are deciding when to press better when we want to be aggressive, we are controlling the transition, and we are much better organised when we have the ball. It's important for us because we are a team that want to play in the opposite half with the ball creating chances, but you know in the Premier League how quick the other attacking players are and you need to control the transitions, second balls. I think we are growing, and improving as a team every week and this is the way."
 On Fulham's three game unbeaten run: "For me, what's important is how we played against a Champions League team in their stadium. My players are believing in the way that we play, and they are fighting, they are improving, they are working. I think we are starting a long journey I hope, I think we will improve, we can do better and for that we will work everyday."
 On saying thank you to supporters: "For me it's really important because we are here for them. This club belongs to them, they are so important, they are travelling so we can feel their support behind us. Today was a good night for everyone because we did well, and I hope they are proud of the team."

 'Not bad but not enough' published at 22:37 GMT 31 October 22:37 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham 
 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa boss Unai Emery speaking to Sky Sports: "Disappointed with the result but a fair result. They deserved
a draw. 
 "In the second half, we were struggling. We started well, trying to dominate, first half we could dominate. We were trying to play with high
pressure.
 "Second half we knew, we should try to play in the same way
as the first half and dominate more but it was completely different. They
started getting chances and they scored. I think the result is fair."
 On Jackson's goal: "He scored a goal, it’s good for him but we didn’t win. I can
analyse, I can speak about the team. The goals are important but the most
important thing is to win the match."
 On Suzuki's mistake: "This is part of football. I think he has played fantastic
and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of
football."
 On wanting consistency from his team: "I still want to see consistency. The last five [Premier League] matches, we
are winning three matches, drawing two. It is not bad but with our poor
start it is not enough.
 "We have to change our mind quick for Tuesday against
Barcelona and then the last match before the international break which is
Manchester United away."
 20 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'This is the start of our journey' published at 22:34 GMT 31 October 22:34 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham 
 Fulham 
 More from Fuham manager Alvaro Arbeloa: "Some really, really clear chances. We had some chances in the first half from counter attacks. But in the second half, from the start we were very demanding as a team and had very clear chances. At the end, we scored in a very lucky way from a cross. But otherwise, we had very clear chances to score more goals. We need to continue working on our finishing and one day, we will score goals easily.
 "The best thing is how we played in the second half because we knew before the end of the match how difficult it is. It doesn't matter. One week ago, Manchester City lost here. It is a Champions League team and I think we saw our character in the second half, how we can play against any team. I think we are a very difficult team to beat and we can beat anyone. You need to believe in yourself, you need to know what team you want to be.
 "We just lost one game in the last four, five or six. But we are doing every week better. We are progressing as a team. We are in a process and we know there will be up and downs. This is the start of a journey, our journey. I'm happy with my players, the way they are working and the way they are playing. We hope to keep improving."
 20 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'That is what I want to see from my team' published at 22:31 GMT 31 October 22:31 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham 
 Fulham 
 Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa speaking to Sky Sports : "I'm so happy with our performance in the second half. This is what I want to see from my team. That character, aggressive and I think we maybe deserved a little bit more but the performance was really great."
 On his message to his players : "I spoke with my players and I was clear because we pressed them man to man. When their players have the ball, you need to be aggressive when you go man to man. For me, that was the main issue in the first half. They were much more aggressive than us. We are a team who want take the ball, control the game through the ball and technically, I think we are very good. But this is the Premier League and you have to be physical and aggressive. You have to be at your best level."
 On Aston Villa's penalty : "I can't talk about referees, or you can pay the fine for me if you want."

 'We could've won the game' published at 22:22 GMT 31 October 22:22 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham 
 Fulham 
 Fulham midfielder Shea Charles speaking to Sky Sports : "Definitely. You could feel a shift in the second half. The way the goal came wasn't how we deserved it really, but positive signs. We could've won the game in the end, but a really good away performance."
 On the message from head coach Alvaro Arbeloa : "It was just to play how we can play. I thought we started quite slow. Giving the ball away in areas we didn't want to. I feel like them right where we wanted them on the press, but then they'd win a duel and be in on goal. I think when we tightened up and recycled the ball and started to play through them, we played really well."
 On teammate Calvin Bassey : "Top player. I don't want to big him up too much, but he's a really good leader. Especially for me coming into the league in my first season. There is no one better to have at the back."
 21 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We will support him' published at 22:17 GMT 31 October 22:17 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham 
 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa defender Ian Maatsen speaking to Sky Sports: "We started the game well. Fulham is a good side, not easy to
win [against] but we came in front. We done well but in the second half we gave them more
time on the ball. They have good players and they can make chances. 
 "We were
unlucky with the goal but we tried to keep fighting. It’s important not to lose
these games.
 On Suzuki's mistake for the goal: "It’s frustrating because don’t want to concede goals but it
can happen to everyone. 
 "Zion is a great guy, great goalkeeper. He will learn
from it. We will support him and go again."
 51 10 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'A good away performance' published at 22:13 GMT 31 October 22:13 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham 
 Fulham 
 Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey speaking to Sky Sports : "I think it was a good away performance. We know how hard it is to come here. It is a difficult place to come, a team with a lot of quality. We wanted a clean sheet, but proud of the boys. They did well."
 On whether they could have got three points instead of one : "I think we should have got more. We missed two chances inside the six-yard box. I know the boys are out there working their socks off to get in the right positions and finishing, we've just got to stay patient and keep trusting in them because we know the quality they have. I just think we could have took all three. A bit unlucky, but we've got to keep positive. Games like this, we've seen in the past where we've been drawing and we've lost. Ipswich, for example.If we can't win, it's very important we don't lose and just happy that we've progressed."
 On Fulham's current form : "100%. Since the start of the season, we've been improving each week and everyone all working hard. Everyone has bought into the way the manager wants to play. We're starting to learn and understand each other. Hopefully, things are going up from now."
